window_overlap_note: Eligible windows overlap; 713 is not 713 independent demonstrations. Prediction comparisons use 3 windows per held-out episode with one fixed prediction seed.
interpretation: All three checkpoints strictly reload and all model parameters are finite; 5000-step optimizer/scheduler state loads and is finite.
Lowest official flow-matching loss belongs to the completed 2k schedule. This does not establish the best robot policy.
4500 steps has the lowest sampled full-chunk joint MAE. 5000 steps has the lowest sampled gripper MAE and first-action joint MAE.

The 2k schedule already decayed learning rate to 2.5e-6; the 20k schedule is incomplete at 5000, with LR approximately 8.57e-5. Different LR schedules prevent attributing differences to step count alone.
One validation increase from 4500 to 5000 does not establish sustained overfitting.

First-action joint errors near 3 degrees are much higher than the 0.23-degree hold-current-state reference, while full-chunk predictions improve over holding state across the full horizon. Review prediction continuity at the beginning of each chunk.
Raw gripper predictions exceed the intended 0–100 mm command range. Bounds and grasp/release timing need independent verification. Clamping alone does not establish task completion.
No physical grasp success, robot tracking performance, unseen-scene generalization or causal camera synchronization was evaluated.
suggested_next_checks: Retain all three candidate checkpoints; compare per-episode and per-horizon action plots before choosing a model.
Prioritize first-action continuity and gripper timing/range checks.
For continued training, keep held-out episodes fixed and use best validation checkpoint selection; 20k is not a required convergence target.
Use a separate controlled robot evaluation only after action-interface and observation-timing checks. No robot actions were sent in this assessment.
